classification.difficultyReason: Read extrema from two graph series and compare their vertical differences across all twelve months.

content.prompt: The line graph below shows the average daily maximum and minimum temperatures for Melbourne.

spec.description: Two connected monthly temperature series above the response parts, with a legend to the right. Maximum temperatures use blue diamonds and minimum temperatures use purple squares; both connecting lines are blue. Source cyan and magenta markers are mapped to standard palette accents.

mathematics.precision: May and September maximum temperatures are graphically estimated, not exact labelled numerical givens.

spec.answerVisibility: All source data, markers, grid, labels and legend remain visible in the question edition; no answers are marked.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In which month(s) is the average daily maximum temperature the highest?

answer.worked: The maximum-temperature series reaches its highest points, about $26^\circ\mathrm{C}$, in January and February.

children.label: b
children.prompt: In which month(s) is the average daily maximum temperature the lowest?

answer.worked: The lowest points on the maximum-temperature series are at $14^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in June and July.

children.label: c
children.prompt: In which month(s) is the average daily minimum temperature the highest?

answer.worked: The minimum-temperature series reaches its highest point, $16^\circ\mathrm{C}$, in February.

children.label: d
children.prompt: In which month(s) is the average daily minimum temperature the lowest?

answer.worked: The lowest points on the minimum-temperature series are at $6^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in June, July and August.

children.label: e
children.prompt: In which month(s) is the difference between average maximum and minimum temperature the greatest?

answer.worked: Compare the vertical gaps between the two series. The greatest gaps occur in January and November: $26-15=11^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $23-12=11^\circ\mathrm{C}$, respectively. Every other month has a smaller gap.

children.label: f
children.prompt: In which month(s) is the difference between average maximum and minimum temperature the least?

answer.worked: Compare the vertical gaps between the two series. May has the smallest gap: approximately $16.5-10=6.5^\circ\mathrm{C}$. September's gap is approximately $16.5-9=7.5^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and all other gaps are larger.
